title: One Hundred Twenty-Nine Thousand Need Water
text:
The Black March nearly failed before seeing Isgard.

Rui stopped the departure when the third fleet ledger reached his table. One hundred twenty-nine thousand people were marching toward the ports. The water calculation covered one hundred nine thousand.

The missing twenty thousand existed everywhere except the arithmetic: physicians, engineers, armour crews, signal keepers, scribes, animal handlers and civilian carriers. Their names filled work rosters. Their thirst had vanished beneath the word support.

[[speaker:rui]]“Nobody boards until the water count matches the body count.”

An imperial general looked toward the harbour mouth. The tide markers were already turning.

“If we miss this window, the main fleet waits six days.”

[[speaker:rui]]“Then we wait six days.”

“Isgard gains six days.”

Rui pushed the ledger back across the table.

[[speaker:rui]]“And if twenty thousand people ration from the first morning, Isgard gains a dying fleet.”

The delay spread through the ports. Soldiers who had slept in armour unloaded casks they had packed twice. Quartermasters reopened sealed stores. Mo’s imperial supply officers discovered their fifty-two-thousand-person calculation assumed land villages could replace spoiled grain. On the Black Current, one wet sack could contaminate a hold before the next shore existed.

Luo rejected two treatment decks because their litter lanes disappeared whenever senior officers unfolded private tables. Yun demanded poison isolation on every seventh vessel instead of one convenient hospital ship an enemy could identify and burn.

[[speaker:yun]]“If all contaminated patients sail together, one sabotage becomes an epidemic.”

The offended admirals lost seven cabins.

By the second night, rain had turned the dock roads to black mud. An axle crushed a porter’s foot. Rhen restored the bones with **Sanctuary of Petals**, then returned the man to a dry shelter rather than the same overloaded cart.

He did not create water. He did not preserve spoiled grain or make an unsafe deck capable of carrying another hundred bodies. Impossible healing waited behind correct preparation instead of replacing it.

Rui walked the final pier before dawn. He opened random casks, counted treatment lanes and made three commanders show where the waste boats would travel when the wind turned south. Only then did he raise the departure flag.

The tide window had closed.

One hundred twenty-nine thousand people still had water.

Every commander left the port understanding the first lesson of continental war: an army could die without an enemy ever arriving.

title: Kael Boards Without Stonecrown
text:
Kael Veyran boarded with one weapon, one travelling case and no personal soldier.

Stonecrown’s fifty thousand watched from the western heights. Two hundred Mountain Nails held bridge joints and buried gates. Eighteen hundred Bastion elites occupied the fortress mouths. Field companies and engineers closed every approach beneath Qin’s contingency map.

The deputy marshal met Kael at the final mountain marker. Grey showed in hair that had been black when Kael first appointed him.

“Sovereign. Final authority.”

He offered a sealed command plate capable of countermanding any Stonecrown order from across the Black Current.

Kael did not take it.

[[speaker:kael]]“Whose gate is the western pass?”

“Mine until your return.”

[[speaker:kael]]“Then why are you giving it away?”

The marshal’s grip tightened around the plate. Five years of exercises had ended the same way: an unexpected report arrived, officers argued, and someone asked what Kael would have done. Kael had begun leaving those questions unanswered. The habit remained harder to kill than any enemy.

“If the invasion exceeds our preparation—”

[[speaker:kael]]“Change the preparation.”

Kael closed the marshal’s fingers over the seal.

[[speaker:kael]]“If every decision waits for my voice across the Black Current, Stonecrown is already defeated.”

Behind them, the gates closed. Iron locks entered channels carved through living mountain. Sand pressure settled into fixed defences only the people remaining knew how to operate. No ceremonial horn accompanied the movement. A supply cart approaching two minutes late was redirected to the lower road without anyone seeking Kael’s permission.

Qin stood beside the marshal rather than above him. Tae’s invisible anchors covered the distant approach. Huo waited outside the command wall because no confirmed hostility yet allowed him inside it.

Kael stepped onto Rui’s vessel.

The gangplank lifted. For the first time in decades, the Mountain crossed a border without bringing the mountain army behind him.

Stonecrown did not follow.

Its gates held anyway.

title: Liang Leaves Twenty Thousand Knives Behind
text:
Liang Yue’s army said farewell without cheering.

Four hundred White-Blood Adjudicators stood in narrow lines beside sixteen hundred Pale Vein Wardens. Behind them waited twelve thousand suppression infantry and six thousand physicians, inspectors and containment troops.

Twenty thousand people remained beneath banners the enemy expected to see sailing north.

Liang walked through the formation once. She corrected one Adjudicator’s hand angle, replaced a Warden whose fever had been hidden beneath cooling powder and removed a restraint spear with a fracture running beneath its grip.

[[speaker:liang]]“If you conceal damage to remain useful, you become damage someone else must survive.”

The Warden surrendered the weapon.

At the central field, two thousand volunteers raised a conventional formation. White Vein’s field elites demonstrated no grand release. Four hundred Adjudicators entered separate circulation rhythms. Sixteen hundred Wardens closed the spaces between them.

The volunteer formation remained conscious. Every soldier retained a weapon. Yet the pathways required to turn two thousand individuals into one military body quietly stopped answering. Command qi reached the wrong joints. Reinforcement stalled before impact. Collective movement separated into harmless steps.

That was why the reserve counted as twenty percent.

[[speaker:liang]]“You remain because Wuyue needs the thing enemies believe I carried away.”

The deputy inspector received Liang’s sealed limitation. Foreign deployment required Qin’s security certification, Liang’s martial authorization and Jin’s campaign order.

“If one seal cannot be reached?”

[[speaker:liang]]“Then you have two reasons to remain.”

“If Stonecrown requests the field elites?”

[[speaker:liang]]“Qin coordinates the request. You decide whether the circulation work is lawful. Kael’s absence does not make his neighbour your owner.”

Liang pressed no farewell blessing into the formation. She left them procedures, refusal rights and the knowledge that her own presence would not return quickly enough to correct a frightened decision.

She boarded alone.

Twenty thousand knives remained sheathed across Wuyue. Their danger came from how little spectacle they required to enter a body—and from the fact that even Liang needed three seals before directing them north.

title: The Fleet Becomes a Moving Country
text:
Rui divided thirty thousand people across warships, transports, grain barges, hospital vessels and ice-supported road platforms.

No ship contained one complete army function. A burned transport could not erase every physician. A captured barge could not take the whole grain reserve. Commanders disliked the inconvenience until Jin placed a black tile over a model vessel and removed every unit assigned to it.

Seven thousand imagined people vanished from the board.

Nobody requested a private command ship afterward.

Mo’s paper signals handled local changes. Jin’s lantern network carried campaign truth between fleets. One delayed lantern meant weather. Two meant route change. Three required confirmation before anyone called it attack. Every dawn, signal crews changed the verification fold so recovered paper could not command tomorrow’s formation.

The Black Current widened until neither shore remained visible. Warships guarded transports. Transports guarded supply barges. River engineers walked across temporary ice roads that cracked behind them and re-formed beneath the next wheels.

At night, the fleet stretched beyond sight. Kitchens burned on water. Physicians changed shifts. Armourers repaired buckles while soldiers slept beneath their benches. Waste boats moved down-current under stricter guard than ceremonial banners.

Sera crossed three decks because one report had taken an hour to travel from the rear line. By the time she arrived, the broken mast had already been replaced and the injured sailors moved.

[[speaker:sera]]“Why was the command signal delayed?”

The local captain pointed toward a lantern boat fighting the cross-current.

“The wind separated it from the verification vessel.”

Jin’s system had prevented a false alarm. It had also made the truth slow.

Sera ordered two smaller verification crews distributed through the rear fleet. She did not abolish confirmation merely because distance had become inconvenient.

Rhen found her on the command deck after midnight. Thousands of lamps moved around them, each carrying people who could not see the campaign centre and still had to trust it existed.

[[speaker:rhen]]“It looks like a country.”

The deck shifted beneath Sera’s feet.

[[speaker:sera]]“Countries have more stable floors.”

A cook shouted that the eastern galley had lost its fire. Three ships answered with covered coals before a commander noticed.

The fleet continued north without ever becoming one vessel an enemy could sink.

title: The First Ships Burn
text:
The first fire vessel appeared inside the rain.

It carried no crew. Black oil covered its forward deck, and its steering chains had been fixed toward the rear supply line. Three more shapes emerged behind it before the warning lantern completed its second swing.

“Fire ships!”

The rear fleet tried to open. Grain barges turned more slowly than warships. One transport swung sideways and trapped the hospital vessel behind it. Rain flattened ordinary flame and spread burning oil across wet rope.

Lei crossed six decks through thunderfire.

He did not strike the hulls. Splintering them would scatter burning timber through the fleet. His first blow broke a steering chain. The second bent an anchor arm until the lead vessel turned past the grain barges. Arin’s disciples reached the rigging below him in teams of three: one blade severed, one redirected the fall, one opened an escape lane for sailors trapped beneath the solution.

A disciple cut too early. Burning canvas dropped across a ladder where six deckhands were climbing.

Arin reversed her sword and caught the mast cloth upon the flat. Heat blackened one sleeve.

[[speaker:arin]]“Look beneath what you save.”

The disciple changed angle. The deckhands escaped.

Another fire vessel struck a grain barge broadside. Rui froze the water around both ships, stopping the collision before it crushed the next transport. Ice crawled up the burning hull and shattered beneath the oil’s heat.

[[speaker:rui]]“Unload the casks. Leave the grain.”

Quartermasters hesitated. Three weeks of medicine lay below the grain deck.

[[speaker:rui]]“Now.”

Soldiers rolled water and treatment casks across the ice. The grain hold ignited before the final medicine chest cleared. Rui released the wreck only when its weight began tearing the frozen road beneath two hospital vessels.

It sank with the remaining food.

At the northern edge, empty skiffs carried Isgard observers away beneath the rain. Lei could reach them. Behind him, a second transport had caught fire.

He turned back.

By dawn, no Sovereign had died. Forty-three sailors and soldiers had. The fleet had lost food, replacement cloth, sail adhesive and medicine that could not be restored by healing the bodies meant to use it.

Jin stood before the wet casualty slate while smoke travelled above the current.

[[speaker:jin]]“They understand armies.”

The Black March continued with less supply and no illusion that Isgard would aim at its strongest faces first.

title: Forty Cross, One Hundred Sixty Remain
text:
Conventional losses made generals look toward Sera’s forty hidden specialists.

One requested Quiet Hands for the next boarding action. Another wanted them placed around command decks as elite guards. A third suggested disguising them as sailors until an enemy committed.

Sera heard all three inside a storage hold that still smelled of smoke.

[[speaker:sera]]“No.”

“We lost forty-three people.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Which is why I will not spend the only anti-sabotage cells we have pretending to be better infantry.”

Seo Dabin placed a strip of sailcloth on the table. Delayed poison had been worked into the adhesive. Heat from the fire ships would have released it across repair crews. Mei Rulan had already found a signal officer replaced two days before departure. Two Wayfinders were opening a route through the wreck field without revealing how they read currents.

None of that work looked like winning a boarding action.

Every part of it kept the fleet alive.

[[speaker:sera]]“The northern cells remain intelligence, medical rescue and anti-sabotage. If an ordinary unit needs reinforcement, command sends an ordinary unit. Hidden strength is not an excuse to stop maintaining visible strength.”

The request seals returned unsigned.

Across the Black Current, the other one hundred sixty Quiet Hands entered their first remote defence field. A marked village stood empty at its centre. Tae and Qin took the attacking side. Huo stood alone with orders to protect the objective without using a full lethal Supreme.

Quiet Hand physicians held stop authority. Signal specialists marked every moment a civilian route would have failed. Scouts changed the village exits while the three great cultivators fought, forcing them to protect people who did not behave like stationary objectives.

The first collision broke three observation towers.

Huo adapted to Tae’s distance and exposed his rear route to Qin’s vibration. Qin exploited the opening and discovered the village evacuation had already moved beneath him. Tae reached the western house and found a Quiet Hand medic refusing to abandon a simulated patient.

No frozen petal entered the operatives’ cultivation.

They improved by watching the three strongest people in the field fail to protect everything at once, then rebuilding the routes those failures exposed.

North of them, forty hidden sleeves moved through a wounded fleet.

South of them, one hundred sixty remained unseen around a village none of Wuyue’s enemies knew mattered.

title: Rhen’s Sanctuary Has a Boundary
text:
The hospital transport began sinking before its distress lantern reached full height.

Eight hundred patients occupied three decks. The fire attack had weakened a repaired seam beneath the waterline. When it failed, the lower ward tilted hard enough to throw litters against one wall.

Rhen crossed the distance without disturbing the ships between.

**Sanctuary of Petals** opened around the transport.

Water stopped inside the broken hull. Pale petals formed an indestructible hemisphere through rain, current and splintered timber. Patients who had begun drowning breathed. Failing hearts stabilized. Broken bones settled before the deck could grind them farther apart.

Then three distress lanterns rose beyond the Sanctuary.

One supply transport had lost steering. A physician deck carried contaminated smoke. A troop ship listed beneath men trapped in armour.

An officer reached Rhen at the upper ward.

“Expand it.”

Rhen’s hand remained on the central support beam. The Sanctuary held hull, water and eight hundred separate lives in one complete circulation.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Then its protection becomes too thin for the ship already breaking.”

“You are Rhen.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“And this is the boundary.”

Outside it, Sera redirected boats toward the listing troop ship. Luo divided physicians between smoke treatment and transfer. Yun sealed the contaminated vessel’s air channels before poison entered its drinking stores. Rui’s engineers raised an ice cradle beneath the hospital keel one rib at a time.

A lower deck tore loose. The Sanctuary received the movement without letting it reach the patients. Rhen could have left the field perfect and permanent. The other ships would have remained outside while everyone waited for him to become four people.

Instead he called the nearest engineer.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Tell me when the hull can carry its own weight.”

The engineer swallowed and inspected the frozen seam with both hands shaking.

Repairs continued for forty-seven minutes. Physicians worked beyond the pale shell with rope, splints and exhausted circulation. One troop ship stabilized. The supply transport was abandoned. Yun’s crews contained the smoke.

“It will hold,” the engineer finally said.

Rhen contracted the Sanctuary by inches. Water tested the repaired hull. The ice cradle took the remaining strain. Eight hundred patients stayed above the current.

The hospital ship survived because an impossible healer and hundreds of ordinary people completed different parts of the same rescue.

Rhen stepped onto the next treatment boat only after the repaired vessel floated without him.

title: Tor Waits at the Northern Shore
text:
Tor Veyrhald waited beneath a white judgment spear at the landing.

Behind him, Isgard formations occupied the cliffs without firing. Shield companies held the upper stone. Skeldran observers watched from rain-dark trees. Rui kept the fleet beyond anchor range while Wuyue’s first landing boats floated between two armies waiting for someone else to become unreasonable.

Sera crossed the final distance with no hidden escort visible.

Tor looked past her toward the black strips crossing six different banners.

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“You destroyed Duskvein under evidence the southern judgment accepted.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Yes.”

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“You returned prisoners. You opened the records. You did not occupy the Guild road.”

[[speaker:sera]]“No.”

His spear remained level.

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“You now enter Isgard with one hundred twenty-nine thousand people.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Because the coalition assembling behind you intends to cross first.”

Tor did not deny it. Officers along the cliff shifted at the silence. Some had expected him to call the fleet imaginary. Others had expected Sera to name pre-emption justice and leave the word invasion to enemies.

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“Intent does not make your landing something other than invasion.”

Sera looked at the narrow beach, the prepared cliff formations and the patients still being moved between vessels behind her.

[[speaker:sera]]“No.”

The agreement disturbed both armies more than propaganda would have.

Tor lowered the spear point by one handspan. One monitored landing lane opened between the cliff formations.

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“Veyrhald grants no passage beyond the Three Gates. This lane exists so wounded and envoys do not drown while our authorities decide which law survives contact.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Then record that Wuyue accepts no Veyrhald command over its army.”

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“Already written.”

The first Wuyue litter crossed the surf beneath Isgard weapons.

No one cheered. No one lowered a shield.

Tor stepped aside only far enough for the monitored road to exist.

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“Enter knowing Isgard will answer.”

Sera walked past the white judgment spear knowing honesty had opened a beach, not peace.

title: Eirholt Draws a White Road
text:
Eira Eirholt drew one white line from the landing to an inland treatment basin.

She used powdered limestone rather than qi. Rain began dissolving its edges before she finished. Eirholt physicians followed with white stakes, canvas screens and handcarts carrying the same medicines to both ends of the road.

[[speaker:eira]]“No armed formation enters. No patient is removed before stable. No army controls the physicians inside.”

Jin looked toward the basin. It offered the cleanest inland route from the beach.

Sera answered before he calculated what occupying it might gain.

[[speaker:sera]]“Agreed.”

Dravaryn refused.

Its officers demanded treatment priority for Isgard soldiers, inspection rights over Wuyue wounded and permission to station cavalry at both exits. Eira listened until the senior officer placed a red seal beside the proposed road.

Then she removed it.

[[speaker:eira]]“Your soldiers may seek another physician.”

“You would deny Isgard treatment for foreigners?”

[[speaker:eira]]“I deny your command over my hands.”

The first wounded arrived before the argument ended. A Wuyue sailor carried an Isgard scout whose skiff had broken beneath Rui’s ice. Two Veyrhald soldiers brought a Silver Horizon disciple burned while cutting rigging. None knew where to stand until Eira pointed at the same intake table.

Luo placed Wuyue healers beside Eirholt staff. Yun opened every medicine case at the boundary and surrendered compounds whose ingredients could not be verified without her.

[[speaker:yun]]“If you cannot identify it, it does not cross.”

Eira nodded once.

Dravaryn cavalry remained beyond the wet white stakes. Wuyue guards stopped at the opposite end. Inside, a physician cut armour from both colours with the same shears.

By sunset, boots and wheels had erased most of the limestone. Eirholt attendants redrew it by lantern light.

The white road belonged to neither continent.

That was why the wounded of both could sleep inside it without one banner deciding who woke first.

title: Wuyue Lands Under Twelve Banners
text:
Wuyue reached Three-Gate Plain beneath twelve Isgard banners.

The coalition occupied the heights in lines extending beyond sight. Veyrhald shields covered the central ridge in pale tiers. Dravaryn cavalry filled the red grasslands east of it. Skeldran hunt markers appeared only when the wind turned their narrow cloth. Six War Banner armies and regional auxiliaries occupied every road Wuyue could use without climbing stone.

Two hundred eighty thousand soldiers turned the ridges into a second horizon.

Below them, Wuyue formed without merging colours. Stormreach held the fast wing. Rui’s river army secured the landing and the shrinking water road behind it. Mo’s imperial centre unfolded through paper signals. Silver Horizon swords gathered beside the Crownless Host without entering its shield structure. Jin’s selected eighteen thousand connected them through lanterns, messengers and roads that had not existed the previous morning.

The columns required six hours to enter position.

Commanders lost sight of their own distant wings. Food carts still came ashore while scouts touched the first gate. One imperial regiment followed a black strip recovered from the mud until a changing paper seal exposed it as Isgard cloth tied over the wrong regional colour. Mo stopped the column three miles before it entered a prepared ravine.

The enemy had already begun learning the Black March.

Sera moved between reports until the numbers stopped behaving like numbers. A delayed water convoy meant thousands unable to cook. One blocked medical road placed the wounded beyond Rhen’s chosen Sanctuary boundary. One cavalry movement on the eastern ridge could be threat, rotation or the first step of an attack arriving before half the army had slept.

Rhen stood beside her without opening a field.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You are counting exits.”

[[speaker:sera]]“There are fewer than the map promised.”

Above them, a thirteenth pole remained empty where Duskvein’s banner had once stood. The absence did not weaken the other twelve enough to make the plain safe.

The final Wuyue formation reached its assigned ground after dark. Lantern signals crossed separate colours. No sealed notice had contained the sound of this many people tightening armour at once.

Jin raised the last campaign marker.

Across the heights, all twelve Isgard banners answered.

The plain between them held long enough for everyone to see the complete army they had previously called an argument.
